cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: If x and y both vary with a third variable t, how can the rate of change of y with respect to x be found?
cards.back: Thus, the rate of change of y with respect to x can be calculated using the rate of change of y and that of x both with respect to t.
cards.quote: Thus, the rate of change of y with respect to x can be calculated using the rate of change of y and that of x both with respect to t.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: What is marginal cost?
cards.back: the instantaneous rate of change of total cost at any level of output
cards.quote: by marginal cost we mean the instantaneous rate of change of total cost at any level of output.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: What is marginal revenue?
cards.back: the rate of change of total revenue with respect to the number of items sold at an instant
cards.quote: by marginal revenue we mean the rate of change of total revenue with respect to the number of items sold at an instant.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Maximum value of f in I: what is the number f (c) called, and what is the point c called?
cards.back: The number f (c) is called the maximum value of f in I and the point c is called a point of maximum value of f in I.
cards.quote: The number f (c) is called the maximum value of f in I and the point c is called a point of maximum value of f in I.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Minimum value of f in I: what is the number f (c) called, and what is the point c called?
cards.back: The number f (c), in this case, is called the minimum value of f in I and the point c, in this case, is called a point of minimum value of f in I.
cards.quote: The number f (c), in this case, is called the minimum value of f in I and the point c, in this case, is called a point of minimum value of f in I.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Define an extreme value of f in I, and name the point c.
cards.back: f is said to have an extreme value in I if there exists a point c in I such that f (c) is either a maximum value or a minimum value of f in I. The number f (c), in this case, is called an extreme value of f in I and the point c is called an extreme point.
cards.quote: f is said to have an extreme value in I if there exists a point c in I such that f (c) is either a maximum value or a minimum value of f in I. The number f (c), in this case, is called an extreme value of f in I and the point c is called an extreme point.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: What is a monotonic function in an interval I?
cards.back: By a monotonic function f in an interval I, we mean that f is either increasing in I or decreasing in I.
cards.quote: By a monotonic function f in an interval I, we mean that f is either increasing in I or decreasing in I.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Where does a monotonic function assume its maximum and minimum values?
cards.back: Every monotonic function assumes its maximum/minimum value at the end points of the domain of definition of the function.
cards.quote: Every monotonic function assumes its maximum/minimum value at the end points of the domain of definition of the function.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: What is true of every continuous function on a closed interval?
cards.back: Every continuous function on a closed interval has a maximum and a minimum value.
cards.quote: Every continuous function on a closed interval has a maximum and a minimum value.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: The local ____ value and local ____ value of the function are referred to as local maxima and local minima, respectively, of the function.
cards.back: The local maximum value and local minimum value of the function are referred to as local maxima and local minima, respectively, of the function.
cards.quote: The local maximum value and local minimum value of the function are referred to as local maxima and local minima, respectively, of the function.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: If c is a point of local maxima of f, what is f (c) called?
cards.back: The value f (c) is called the local maximum value of f.
cards.quote: The value f (c) is called the local maximum value of f.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: If c is a point of local minima of f, what is f (c) called?
cards.back: The value f (c) is called the local minimum value of f.
cards.quote: The value f (c) is called the local minimum value of f.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Is every point where the derivative vanishes a point of local maxima or local minima?
cards.back: The converse of above theorem need not be true, that is, a point at which the derivative vanishes need not be a point of local maxima or local minima.
cards.quote: The converse of above theorem need not be true, that is, a point at which the derivative vanishes need not be a point of local maxima or local minima.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: First Derivative Test: what if the derivative does not change sign as x increases through c?
cards.back: If f ′(x) does not change sign as x increases through c, then c is neither a point of local maxima nor a point of local minima. Infact, such a point is called point of inflection.
cards.quote: If f ′(x) does not change sign as x increases through c, then c is neither a point of local maxima nor a point of local minima. Infact, such a point is called point of inflection.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: What does "f is twice differentiable at c" mean?
cards.back: As f is twice differentiable at c, we mean second order derivative of f exists at c.
cards.quote: As f is twice differentiable at c, we mean second order derivative of f exists at c.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: What other names are given to the absolute maximum value of f on an interval?
cards.back: absolute maximum value (global maximum or greatest value)
cards.quote: is called absolute maximum value (global maximum or greatest value) of f on the interval [0, 1].

source.section: Maximum and Minimum Values of a Function in a Closed Interval

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: What other names are given to the absolute minimum value of f on an interval?
cards.back: absolute minimum value (global minimum or least value)
cards.quote: is called the absolute minimum value (global minimum or least value) of f on [0, 1].

source.section: Maximum and Minimum Values of a Function in a Closed Interval

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Theorem 5: what is true of a continuous function f on the interval [a, b]?
cards.back: Let f be a continuous function on an interval I = [a, b]. Then f has the absolute maximum value and f attains it at least once in I. Also, f has the absolute minimum value and attains it at least once in I.
cards.quote: Let f be a continuous function on an interval I = [a, b]. Then f has the absolute maximum value and f attains it at least once in I. Also, f has the absolute minimum value and attains it at least once in I.

source.section: Maximum and Minimum Values of a Function in a Closed Interval

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Elementary geometry formulae cannot give areas enclosed by curves. What do we need for that?
cards.back: However, they are inadequate for calculating the areas enclosed by curves. For that we shall need some concepts of Integral Calculus.
cards.quote: However, they are inadequate for calculating the areas enclosed by curves. For that we shall need some concepts of Integral Calculus.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: In this chapter, areas between lines and arcs of which curves are studied?
cards.back: area between lines and arcs of circles, parabolas and ellipses (standard forms only)
cards.quote: area between lines and arcs of circles, parabolas and ellipses (standard forms only)

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: How can the area under a curve be thought of, when finding it by integration (Fig 8.1)?
cards.back: From Fig 8.1, we can think of area under the curve as composed of large number of very thin vertical strips.
cards.quote: From Fig 8.1, we can think of area under the curve as composed of large number of very thin vertical strips.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: For the area bounded by a curve, the y-axis and two horizontal lines (Fig 8.2), which strips are considered?
cards.back: Here, we consider horizontal strips as shown in the Fig 8.2
cards.quote: Here, we consider horizontal strips as shown in the Fig 8.2

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Example 1: why is the whole area of the circle taken as 4 times the area of the region in the first quadrant?
cards.back: as the circle is symmetrical about both x-axis and y-axis
cards.quote: as the circle is symmetrical about both x-axis and y-axis

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Naively, when is a function continuous at a fixed point?
cards.back: Naively, we may say that a function is continuous at a fixed point if we can draw the graph of the function around that point without lifting the pen from the plane of the paper.
cards.quote: Naively, we may say that a function is continuous at a fixed point if we can draw the graph of the function around that point without lifting the pen from the plane of the paper.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Define: when is a function continuous at x = c (in words)?
cards.back: a function is continuous at x = c if the function is defined at x = c and if the value of the function at x = c equals the limit of the function at x = c.
cards.quote: a function is continuous at x = c if the function is defined at x = c and if the value of the function at x = c equals the limit of the function at x = c.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: More elaborately, when is f said to be continuous at x = c?
cards.back: More elaborately, if the left hand limit, right hand limit and the value of the function at x = c exist and equal to each other, then f is said to be continuous at x = c.
cards.quote: More elaborately, if the left hand limit, right hand limit and the value of the function at x = c exist and equal to each other, then f is said to be continuous at x = c.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: What is the limit of a function at x = c when the right and left hand limits coincide?
cards.back: Recall that if the right hand and left hand limits at x = c coincide, then we say that the common value is the limit of the function at x = c.
cards.quote: Recall that if the right hand and left hand limits at x = c coincide, then we say that the common value is the limit of the function at x = c.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Define a point of discontinuity of f.
cards.back: If f is not continuous at c, we say f is discontinuous at c and c is called a point of discontinuity of f.
cards.quote: If f is not continuous at c, we say f is discontinuous at c and c is called a point of discontinuity of f.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Define a continuous function (Definition 2).
cards.back: A real function f is said to be continuous if it is continuous at every point in the domain of f.
cards.quote: A real function f is said to be continuous if it is continuous at every point in the domain of f.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: What is needed for f on a closed interval [a, b] to be continuous?
cards.back: Suppose f is a function defined on a closed interval [a, b], then for f to be continuous, it needs to be continuous at every point in [a, b] including the end points a and b.
cards.quote: Suppose f is a function defined on a closed interval [a, b], then for f to be continuous, it needs to be continuous at every point in [a, b] including the end points a and b.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: If f is defined at only one point, is it continuous?
cards.back: if f is defined only at one point, it is continuous there, i.e., if the domain of f is a singleton, f is a continuous function.
cards.quote: if f is defined only at one point, it is continuous there, i.e., if the domain of f is a singleton, f is a continuous function.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Are the sine and cosine functions continuous?
cards.back: We have just proved that both sine and cosine functions are continuous.
cards.quote: We have just proved that both sine and cosine functions are continuous.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Why is tan x continuous wherever it is defined?
cards.back: Thus tan x being a quotient of two continuous functions is continuous wherever it is defined.
cards.quote: Thus tan x being a quotient of two continuous functions is continuous wherever it is defined.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: When is a function differentiable in an interval [a, b]?
cards.back: A function is said to be differentiable in an interval [a, b] if it is differentiable at every point of [a, b].
cards.quote: A function is said to be differentiable in an interval [a, b] if it is differentiable at every point of [a, b].

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: State Theorem 3: relation between differentiability and continuity at a point.
cards.back: If a function f is differentiable at a point c, then it is also continuous at that point.
cards.quote: If a function f is differentiable at a point c, then it is also continuous at that point.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: ____ is rule to differentiate composites of functions.
cards.back: Chain rule is rule to differentiate composites of functions.
cards.quote: Chain rule is rule to differentiate composites of functions.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: When is y said to be given as an explicit function of x?
cards.back: When a relationship between x and y is expressed in a way that it is easy to solve for y and write y = f (x), we say that y is given as an explicit function of x.
cards.quote: When a relationship between x and y is expressed in a way that it is easy to solve for y and write y = f (x), we say that y is given as an explicit function of x.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: On what does the growth of polynomial functions depend?
cards.back: the growth of polynomial functions is dependent on the degree of the polynomial function - higher the degree, greater is the growth.
cards.quote: the growth of polynomial functions is dependent on the degree of the polynomial function - higher the degree, greater is the growth.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: What is the domain of the exponential function?
cards.back: Domain of the exponential function is R, the set of all real numbers.
cards.quote: Domain of the exponential function is R, the set of all real numbers.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Range of the exponential function is the set of all ____ real numbers.
cards.back: Range of the exponential function is the set of all positive real numbers.
cards.quote: Range of the exponential function is the set of all positive real numbers.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: The point ____ is always on the graph of the exponential function
cards.back: The point (0, 1) is always on the graph of the exponential function
cards.quote: The point (0, 1) is always on the graph of the exponential function

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Exponential function is ever ____; i.e., as we move from left to right, the graph rises above.
cards.back: Exponential function is ever increasing; i.e., as we move from left to right, the graph rises above.
cards.quote: Exponential function is ever increasing; i.e., as we move from left to right, the graph rises above.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: What happens to the graph of the exponential function for very large negative x?
cards.back: For very large negative values of x, the exponential function is very close to 0. In other words, in the second quadrant, the graph approaches x-axis (but never meets it).
cards.quote: For very large negative values of x, the exponential function is very close to 0. In other words, in the second quadrant, the graph approaches x-axis (but never meets it).

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Exponential function with base 10 is called the ____.
cards.back: Exponential function with base 10 is called the common exponential function.
cards.quote: Exponential function with base 10 is called the common exponential function.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: What is the exponential function with the number e as its base called?
cards.back: This is called natural exponential function.
cards.quote: This is called natural exponential function.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: What are logarithms to base 10 and to base e called?
cards.back: As before if the base b = 10, we say it is common logarithms and if b = e, then we say it is natural logarithms.
cards.quote: As before if the base b = 10, we say it is common logarithms and if b = e, then we say it is natural logarithms.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Often natural logarithm is denoted by ____.
cards.back: Often natural logarithm is denoted by ln.
cards.quote: Often natural logarithm is denoted by ln.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: In this chapter, what does log x denote?
cards.back: In this chapter, log x denotes the logarithm function to base e, i.e., ln x will be written as simply log x.
cards.quote: In this chapter, log x denotes the logarithm function to base e, i.e., ln x will be written as simply log x.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: How are the graphs of the natural exponential function and ln x related?
cards.back: It is of interest to observe that the two curves are the mirror images of each other reflected in the line y = x.
cards.quote: It is of interest to observe that the two curves are the mirror images of each other reflected in the line y = x.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: One of the striking properties of the ____ in differential calculus is that it doesn't change during the process of differentiation.
cards.back: One of the striking properties of the natural exponential function in differential calculus is that it doesn't change during the process of differentiation.
cards.quote: One of the striking properties of the natural exponential function in differential calculus is that it doesn't change during the process of differentiation.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: When is the relation between two variables expressed via a third variable?
cards.back: Sometimes the relation between two variables is neither explicit nor implicit, but some link of a third variable with each of the two variables, separately, establishes a relation between the first two variables.
cards.quote: Sometimes the relation between two variables is neither explicit nor implicit, but some link of a third variable with each of the two variables, separately, establishes a relation between the first two variables.

source.section: Derivatives of Functions in Parametric Forms

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Define parametric form of a relation between x and y.
cards.back: More precisely, a relation expressed between two variables x and y in the form x = f (t), y = g (t) is said to be parametric form with t as a parameter.
cards.quote: More precisely, a relation expressed between two variables x and y in the form x = f (t), y = g (t) is said to be parametric form with t as a parameter.

source.section: Derivatives of Functions in Parametric Forms

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: How may the determinant be thought of as a function on square matrices?
cards.back: a function which associates each square matrix with a unique number (real or complex)
cards.quote: a function which associates each square matrix with a unique number (real or complex)

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Is the vertical-bar notation for a matrix A read as the determinant of A or as the modulus of A?
cards.back: read as determinant of A and not modulus of A
cards.quote: read as determinant of A and not modulus of A

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Only ____ matrices have determinants.
cards.back: Only square matrices have determinants.
cards.quote: Only square matrices have determinants.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: What is expansion of a determinant along a row (or a column)?
cards.back: Determinant of a matrix of order three can be determined by expressing it in terms of second order determinants. This is known as expansion of a determinant along a row (or a column).
cards.quote: Determinant of a matrix of order three can be determined by expressing it in terms of second order determinants. This is known as expansion of a determinant along a row (or a column).

source.section: Determinant of a matrix of order 3 x 3

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: What happens to the value of a determinant if it is expanded along a different row or column?
cards.back: expanding a determinant along any row or column gives same value
cards.quote: expanding a determinant along any row or column gives same value

source.section: Determinant of a matrix of order 3 x 3

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: For easier calculations, we shall expand the determinant along that row or column which contains maximum number of ____.
cards.back: For easier calculations, we shall expand the determinant along that row or column which contains maximum number of zeros.
cards.quote: For easier calculations, we shall expand the determinant along that row or column which contains maximum number of zeros.

source.section: Determinant of a matrix of order 3 x 3

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: The area of the triangle formed by three ____ points is zero.
cards.back: The area of the triangle formed by three collinear points is zero.
cards.quote: The area of the triangle formed by three collinear points is zero.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: How is the value of a determinant obtained from cofactors?
cards.back: Value of determinant of a matrix A is obtained by sum of product of elements of a row (or a column) with corresponding cofactors.
cards.quote: Value of determinant of a matrix A is obtained by sum of product of elements of a row (or a column) with corresponding cofactors.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: What is the sum when the elements of one row (or column) are multiplied with the cofactors of another row (or column)?
cards.back: If elements of one row (or column) are multiplied with cofactors of elements of any other row (or column), then their sum is zero.
cards.quote: If elements of one row (or column) are multiplied with cofactors of elements of any other row (or column), then their sum is zero.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Adjoint of the matrix A is denoted by ____.
cards.back: Adjoint of the matrix A is denoted by adj A.
cards.quote: Adjoint of the matrix A is denoted by adj A.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: When is a square matrix said to be singular?
cards.back: A square matrix A is said to be singular if | A | = 0.
cards.quote: A square matrix A is said to be singular if | A | = 0.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: When is a square matrix said to be non-singular?
cards.back: A square matrix A is said to be non-singular if | A | ≠ 0
cards.quote: A square matrix A is said to be non-singular if | A | ≠ 0

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: A square matrix A is said to be ____ if | A | = 0.
cards.back: A square matrix A is said to be singular if | A | = 0.
cards.quote: A square matrix A is said to be singular if | A | = 0.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: If A and B are nonsingular matrices of the same order, what can be said of AB and BA?
cards.back: If A and B are nonsingular matrices of the same order, then AB and BA are also nonsingular matrices of the same order.
cards.quote: If A and B are nonsingular matrices of the same order, then AB and BA are also nonsingular matrices of the same order.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: State the product theorem for determinants of square matrices of the same order.
cards.back: The determinant of the product of matrices is equal to product of their respective determinants
cards.quote: The determinant of the product of matrices is equal to product of their respective determinants

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: When is a square matrix invertible?
cards.back: A square matrix A is invertible if and only if A is nonsingular matrix.
cards.quote: A square matrix A is invertible if and only if A is nonsingular matrix.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: When is a square matrix B called the inverse of A?
cards.back: If AB = BA = I, where B is square matrix, then B is called inverse of A.
cards.quote: If AB = BA = I, where B is square matrix, then B is called inverse of A.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: What is a consistent system of equations?
cards.back: A system of equations is said to be consistent if its solution (one or more) exists.
cards.quote: A system of equations is said to be consistent if its solution (one or more) exists.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: What is an inconsistent system of equations?
cards.back: A system of equations is said to be inconsistent if its solution does not exist.
cards.quote: A system of equations is said to be inconsistent if its solution does not exist.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: A system of equations is said to be ____ if its solution (one or more) exists.
cards.back: A system of equations is said to be consistent if its solution (one or more) exists.
cards.quote: A system of equations is said to be consistent if its solution (one or more) exists.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: A system of equations is said to be ____ if its solution does not exist.
cards.back: A system of equations is said to be inconsistent if its solution does not exist.
cards.quote: A system of equations is said to be inconsistent if its solution does not exist.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: What is the method of solving a system of equations using the inverse of the coefficient matrix called?
cards.back: This method of solving system of equations is known as Matrix Method.
cards.quote: This method of solving system of equations is known as Matrix Method.

source.section: Solution of system of linear equations using inverse of a matrix

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: If A is singular and (adj A) B is not the zero matrix, what is the nature of the system AX = B?
cards.back: then solution does not exist and the system of equations is called inconsistent
cards.quote: then solution does not exist and the system of equations is called inconsistent

source.section: Solution of system of linear equations using inverse of a matrix

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: For AX = B with A a square matrix, what follows when | A | ≠ 0?
cards.back: there exists unique solution
cards.quote: there exists unique solution

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: For AX = B, what follows when | A | = 0 and (adj A) B is not the zero matrix?
cards.back: then there exists no solution
cards.quote: then there exists no solution

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: For AX = B, what follows when | A | = 0 and (adj A) B is the zero matrix?
cards.back: then system may or may not be consistent
cards.quote: then system may or may not be consistent

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: What is a differential equation?
cards.back: In general, an equation involving derivative (derivatives) of the dependent variable with respect to independent variable (variables) is called a differential equation.
cards.quote: In general, an equation involving derivative (derivatives) of the dependent variable with respect to independent variable (variables) is called a differential equation.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: An equation involving ____ of the dependent variable with respect to independent variable (variables) is known as a differential equation.
cards.back: An equation involving derivatives of the dependent variable with respect to independent variable (variables) is known as a differential equation.
cards.quote: An equation involving derivatives of the dependent variable with respect to independent variable (variables) is known as a differential equation.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Define an ordinary differential equation.
cards.back: A differential equation involving derivatives of the dependent variable with respect to only one independent variable is called an ordinary differential equation
cards.quote: A differential equation involving derivatives of the dependent variable with respect to only one independent variable is called an ordinary differential equation

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Define partial differential equations.
cards.back: differential equations involving derivatives with respect to more than one independent variables, called partial differential equations
cards.quote: there are differential equations involving derivatives with respect to more than one independent variables, called partial differential equations

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Define the order of a differential equation.
cards.back: Order of a differential equation is defined as the order of the highest order derivative of the dependent variable with respect to the independent variable involved in the given differential equation.
cards.quote: Order of a differential equation is defined as the order of the highest order derivative of the dependent variable with respect to the independent variable involved in the given differential equation.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Order of a differential equation is the order of the ____ occurring in the differential equation.
cards.back: Order of a differential equation is the order of the highest order derivative occurring in the differential equation.
cards.quote: Order of a differential equation is the order of the highest order derivative occurring in the differential equation.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: To study the degree of a differential equation, the key point is that the differential equation must be a ____
cards.back: To study the degree of a differential equation, the key point is that the differential equation must be a polynomial equation in derivatives
cards.quote: To study the degree of a differential equation, the key point is that the differential equation must be a polynomial equation in derivatives

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Define the degree of a differential equation (when it is a polynomial equation in derivatives).
cards.back: By the degree of a differential equation, when it is a polynomial equation in derivatives, we mean the highest power (positive integral index) of the highest order derivative involved in the given differential equation.
cards.quote: By the degree of a differential equation, when it is a polynomial equation in derivatives, we mean the highest power (positive integral index) of the highest order derivative involved in the given differential equation.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Degree of a differential equation is defined if it is a ____ in its derivatives.
cards.back: Degree of a differential equation is defined if it is a polynomial equation in its derivatives.
cards.quote: Degree of a differential equation is defined if it is a polynomial equation in its derivatives.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Degree (when defined) of a differential equation is the ____ (positive integer only) of the highest order derivative in it.
cards.back: Degree (when defined) of a differential equation is the highest power (positive integer only) of the highest order derivative in it.
cards.quote: Degree (when defined) of a differential equation is the highest power (positive integer only) of the highest order derivative in it.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Order and degree (if defined) of a differential equation are always ____.
cards.back: Order and degree (if defined) of a differential equation are always positive integers.
cards.quote: Order and degree (if defined) of a differential equation are always positive integers.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: What is a solution of a differential equation?
cards.back: A function which satisfies the given differential equation is called its solution.
cards.quote: A function which satisfies the given differential equation is called its solution.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Define the general solution (primitive) of a differential equation.
cards.back: The solution which contains arbitrary constants is called the general solution (primitive) of the differential equation.
cards.quote: The solution which contains arbitrary constants is called the general solution (primitive) of the differential equation.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Define a particular solution of a differential equation.
cards.back: The solution free from arbitrary constants i.e., the solution obtained from the general solution by giving particular values to the arbitrary constants is called a particular solution of the differential equation.
cards.quote: The solution free from arbitrary constants i.e., the solution obtained from the general solution by giving particular values to the arbitrary constants is called a particular solution of the differential equation.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: How many arbitrary constants does the general solution of a differential equation contain?
cards.back: The solution which contains as many arbitrary constants as the order of the differential equation is called a general solution
cards.quote: The solution which contains as many arbitrary constants as the order of the differential equation is called a general solution and the solution free from arbitrary constants is called particular solution.
cards.note: A fourth order equation has 4 constants in its general solution; a particular solution has none.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: When is the variable separable method used to solve a differential equation?
cards.back: Variable separable method is used to solve such an equation in which variables can be separated completely i.e. terms containing y should remain with dy and terms containing x should remain with dx.
cards.quote: Variable separable method is used to solve such an equation in which variables can be separated completely i.e. terms containing y should remain with dy and terms containing x should remain with dx.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: A first order differential equation is said to be homogeneous if the function giving its derivative is a homogeneous function of which degree?
cards.back: homogenous function of degree zero
cards.quote: is a homogenous function of degree zero

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: In solving a first order linear differential equation, what is the multiplying function that makes the left side a derivative called?
cards.back: Integrating Factor (I.F.)
cards.quote: is called Integrating Factor (I.F.) of the given differential equation

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: What are anti derivatives (or primitives) of a function?
cards.back: The functions that could possibly have given function as a derivative are called anti derivatives (or primitive) of the function.
cards.quote: The functions that could possibly have given function as a derivative are called anti derivatives (or primitive) of the function.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Which two forms of integrals together constitute Integral Calculus?
cards.back: indefinite and definite integrals
cards.quote: These two problems lead to the two forms of the integrals, e.g., indefinite and definite integrals, which together constitute the Integral Calculus.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Name the two types of problems that led to the development of integral calculus.
cards.back:
(a) the problem of finding a function whenever its derivative is given,
(b) the problem of finding the area bounded by the graph of a function under certain conditions.
cards.quote: (a) the problem of finding a function whenever its derivative is given, (b) the problem of finding the area bounded by the graph of a function under certain conditions.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Differential Calculus is centred on the concept of the ____.
cards.back: Differential Calculus is centred on the concept of the derivative.
cards.quote: Differential Calculus is centred on the concept of the derivative.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Integral Calculus is motivated by the problem of defining and calculating the ____ of the region bounded by the graph of the functions.
cards.back: Integral Calculus is motivated by the problem of defining and calculating the area of the region bounded by the graph of the functions.
cards.quote: Integral Calculus is motivated by the problem of defining and calculating the area of the region bounded by the graph of the functions.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: There is a connection, known as the ____, between indefinite integral and definite integral
cards.back: There is a connection, known as the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, between indefinite integral and definite integral
cards.quote: There is a connection, known as the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, between indefinite integral and definite integral

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: What is integration?
cards.back: Integration is the inverse process of differentiation.
cards.quote: Integration is the inverse process of differentiation.

source.section: 7.2 Integration as an Inverse Process of Differentiation

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: What is the process of finding the primitive of a given derivative called?
cards.back: Such a process is called integration or anti differentiation.
cards.quote: Such a process is called integration or anti differentiation.

source.section: 7.2 Integration as an Inverse Process of Differentiation

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: What is C customarily referred to as, in the family of anti derivatives?
cards.back: For this reason C is customarily referred to as arbitrary constant.
cards.quote: For this reason C is customarily referred to as arbitrary constant.

source.section: 7.2 Integration as an Inverse Process of Differentiation

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Functions with same derivatives differ by a ____.
cards.back: Functions with same derivatives differ by a constant.
cards.quote: Functions with same derivatives differ by a constant.

source.section: 7.2 Integration as an Inverse Process of Differentiation

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: The process of differentiation and integration are ____ of each other in the sense of the following results
cards.back: The process of differentiation and integration are inverses of each other in the sense of the following results
cards.quote: The process of differentiation and integration are inverses of each other in the sense of the following results

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: The search for the requisite function for finding an anti derivative is known as integration by the ____.
cards.back: The search for the requisite function for finding an anti derivative is known as integration by the method of inspection.
cards.quote: The search for the requisite function for finding an anti derivative is known as integration by the method of inspection.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Which functions are called elementary functions (Remark ii)?
cards.back: polynomial, logarithmic, exponential, trigonometric functions and their inverses etc.
cards.quote: Sometimes, F is not expressible in terms of elementary functions viz., polynomial, logarithmic, exponential, trigonometric functions and their inverses etc.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Name the three prominent methods of integration.
cards.back:
1. Integration by Substitution
2. Integration using Partial Fractions
3. Integration by Parts
cards.quote: Prominent among them are methods based on: 1. Integration by Substitution 2. Integration using Partial Fractions 3. Integration by Parts

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Usually, we make a substitution for a function whose ____ also occurs in the integrand as illustrated in the following examples.
cards.back: Usually, we make a substitution for a function whose derivative also occurs in the integrand as illustrated in the following examples.
cards.quote: Usually, we make a substitution for a function whose derivative also occurs in the integrand as illustrated in the following examples.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: The method in which we change the variable to some other variable is called the ____.
cards.back: The method in which we change the variable to some other variable is called the method of substitution.
cards.quote: The method in which we change the variable to some other variable is called the method of substitution.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: The improper rational functions can be reduced to the proper rational functions by ____ process.
cards.back: The improper rational functions can be reduced to the proper rational functions by long division process.
cards.quote: The improper rational functions can be reduced to the proper rational functions by long division process.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: The rational functions which we shall consider here for integration purposes will be those whose denominators can be factorised into ____.
cards.back: The rational functions which we shall consider here for integration purposes will be those whose denominators can be factorised into linear and quadratic factors.
cards.quote: The rational functions which we shall consider here for integration purposes will be those whose denominators can be factorised into linear and quadratic factors.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: The equation (1) above is an ____, i.e. a statement true for all (permissible) values of x.
cards.back: The equation (1) above is an identity, i.e. a statement true for all (permissible) values of x.
cards.quote: The equation (1) above is an identity, i.e. a statement true for all (permissible) values of x.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: In this section, we describe one more method of integration, that is found quite useful in integrating ____.
cards.back: In this section, we describe one more method of integration, that is found quite useful in integrating products of functions.
cards.quote: In this section, we describe one more method of integration, that is found quite useful in integrating products of functions.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Which functions are usually taken as the first function in integration by parts?
cards.back: Usually, if any function is a power of x or a polynomial in x, then we take it as the first function. However, in cases where other function is inverse trigonometric function or logarithmic function, then we take them as first function.
cards.quote: Usually, if any function is a power of x or a polynomial in x, then we take it as the first function. However, in cases where other function is inverse trigonometric function or logarithmic function, then we take them as first function.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: In finding the integral of log x by parts, which function is first and which is second?
cards.back: We take log x as the first function and the constant function 1 as the second function.
cards.quote: We take log x as the first function and the constant function 1 as the second function.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: In a definite integral from a to b, what are a and b called?
cards.back: are called the limits of integration, a being the lower limit and b the upper limit.
cards.quote: are called the limits of integration, a being the lower limit and b the upper limit.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: How is the definite integral introduced, and what is its value when F is an anti derivative?
cards.back: The definite integral is introduced either as the limit of a sum or if it has an anti derivative F in the interval [a, b], then its value is the difference between the values of F at the end points
cards.quote: The definite integral is introduced either as the limit of a sum or if it has an anti derivative F in the interval [a, b], then its value is the difference between the values of F at the end points

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: First fundamental theorem of integral calculus: what is assumed about f?
cards.back: Let f be a continuous function on the closed interval [a, b] and let A (x) be the area function.
cards.quote: Let f be a continuous function on the closed interval [a, b] and let A (x) be the area function.
cards.note: Conclusion: the derivative of the area function A(x) equals f(x) for every x in [a, b].

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: We state below an important theorem which enables us to evaluate definite integrals by making use of ____.
cards.back: We state below an important theorem which enables us to evaluate definite integrals by making use of anti derivative.
cards.quote: We state below an important theorem which enables us to evaluate definite integrals by making use of anti derivative.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Second fundamental theorem of integral calculus: what is assumed about f and F?
cards.back: Let f be continuous function defined on the closed interval [a, b] and F be an anti derivative of f.
cards.quote: Let f be continuous function defined on the closed interval [a, b] and F be an anti derivative of f.
cards.note: Conclusion: the definite integral of f from a to b equals F(b) minus F(a).

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: The crucial operation in evaluating a definite integral is that of finding a function whose derivative is equal to the ____.
cards.back: The crucial operation in evaluating a definite integral is that of finding a function whose derivative is equal to the integrand.
cards.quote: The crucial operation in evaluating a definite integral is that of finding a function whose derivative is equal to the integrand.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: What must hold for f in a definite integral over [a, b] (Second theorem, Remark iv)?
cards.back: the function f needs to be well defined and continuous in [a, b].
cards.quote: the function f needs to be well defined and continuous in [a, b].

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Steps to evaluate a definite integral by substitution, in order.
cards.back:
1. Consider the integral without limits and substitute, y = f (x) or x = g(y) to reduce the given integral to a known form.
2. Integrate the new integrand with respect to the new variable without mentioning the constant of integration.
3. Resubstitute for the new variable and write the answer in terms of the original variable.
4. Find the values of answers obtained in (3) at the given limits of integral and find the difference of the values at the upper and lower limits.
cards.quote: 1. Consider the integral without limits and substitute, y = f (x) or x = g(y) to reduce the given integral to a known form. 2. Integrate the new integrand with respect to the new variable without mentioning the constant of integration. 3. Resubstitute for the new variable and write the answer in terms of the original variable. 4. Find the values of answers obtained in (3) at the given limits of integral and find the difference of the values at the upper and lower limits.

source.section: 7.9 Evaluation of Definite Integrals by Substitution

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: If g is the inverse of f, how are the domain and range of g related to those of f?
cards.back: Here, the domain of g = range of f and the range of g = domain of f.
cards.quote: Here, the domain of g = range of f and the range of g = domain of f.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: What are the domain and range of the sine function?
cards.back: the domain of sine function is the set of all real numbers and range is the closed interval [-1, 1]
cards.quote: Since the domain of sine function is the set of all real numbers and range is the closed interval [-1, 1].

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: If (a, b) is a point on the graph of the sine function, what is the corresponding point on the graph of its inverse?
cards.back: then (b, a) becomes the corresponding point on the graph of inverse of sine function.
cards.quote: if (a, b) is a point on the graph of sine function, then (b, a) becomes the corresponding point on the graph of inverse of sine function.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: What are the domain and range of the cosine function?
cards.back: the cosine function is a function whose domain is the set of all real numbers and range is the set [-1, 1]
cards.quote: Like sine function, the cosine function is a function whose domain is the set of all real numbers and range is the set [-1, 1].

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: What is the principal value of an inverse trigonometric function?
cards.back: The value of an inverse trigonometric functions which lies in the range of principal branch is called the principal value of that inverse trigonometric functions.
cards.quote: The value of an inverse trigonometric functions which lies in the range of principal branch is called the principal value of that inverse trigonometric functions.
cards.note: The principal value is the value that lies in the range of the principal value branch.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Whenever no branch of an inverse trigonometric functions is mentioned, we mean the ____ value branch of that function.
cards.back: Whenever no branch of an inverse trigonometric functions is mentioned, we mean the principal value branch of that function.
cards.quote: Whenever no branch of an inverse trigonometric functions is mentioned, we mean the principal value branch of that function.
cards.note: If no branch is named, the principal value branch is meant.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: A special but a very important class of optimisation problems is ____.
cards.back: A special but a very important class of optimisation problems is linear programming problem.
cards.quote: A special but a very important class of optimisation problems is linear programming problem.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Define a linear programming problem.
cards.back: Thus, a Linear Programming Problem is one that is concerned with finding the optimal value (maximum or minimum value) of a linear function (called objective function) of several variables (say x and y), subject to the conditions that the variables are non-negative and satisfy a set of linear inequalities (called linear constraints).
cards.quote: Thus, a Linear Programming Problem is one that is concerned with finding the optimal value (maximum or minimum value) of a linear function (called objective function) of several variables (say x and y), subject to the conditions that the variables are non-negative and satisfy a set of linear inequalities (called linear constraints).

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: What do the terms linear and programming mean in a linear programming problem?
cards.back: The term linear implies that all the mathematical relations used in the problem are linear relations while the term programming refers to the method of determining a particular programme or plan of action.
cards.quote: The term linear implies that all the mathematical relations used in the problem are linear relations while the term programming refers to the method of determining a particular programme or plan of action.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Variables x and y are called ____.
cards.back: Variables x and y are called decision variables.
cards.quote: Variables x and y are called decision variables.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: What are constraints in a linear programming problem?
cards.back: The linear inequalities or equations or restrictions on the variables of a linear programming problem are called constraints.
cards.quote: The linear inequalities or equations or restrictions on the variables of a linear programming problem are called constraints.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: What is an infeasible region?
cards.back: The region other than feasible region is called an infeasible region.
cards.quote: The region other than feasible region is called an infeasible region.

source.section: Graphical method of solving linear programming problems

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: What are feasible solutions of a linear programming problem?
cards.back: Points within and on the boundary of the feasible region represent feasible solutions of the constraints.
cards.quote: Points within and on the boundary of the feasible region represent feasible solutions of the constraints.

source.section: Graphical method of solving linear programming problems

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: What is an infeasible solution?
cards.back: Any point outside the feasible region is called an infeasible solution.
cards.quote: Any point outside the feasible region is called an infeasible solution.

source.section: Graphical method of solving linear programming problems

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: What is an optimal (feasible) solution?
cards.back: Any point in the feasible region that gives the optimal value (maximum or minimum) of the objective function is called an optimal solution.
cards.quote: Any point in the feasible region that gives the optimal value (maximum or minimum) of the objective function is called an optimal solution.

source.section: Graphical method of solving linear programming problems

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Theorem 2: what happens to the objective function if the feasible region R is bounded?
cards.back: the objective function Z has both a maximum and a minimum value on R and each of these occurs at a corner point (vertex) of R.
cards.quote: then the objective function Z has both a maximum and a minimum value on R and each of these occurs at a corner point (vertex) of R.

source.section: Graphical method of solving linear programming problems

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: If the feasible region R is unbounded, will a maximum or minimum of the objective function always exist?
cards.back: If R is unbounded, then a maximum or a minimum value of the objective function may not exist. However, if it exists, it must occur at a corner point of R.
cards.quote: If R is unbounded, then a maximum or a minimum value of the objective function may not exist. However, if it exists, it must occur at a corner point of R.

source.section: Graphical method of solving linear programming problems

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: What is a corner point of a feasible region?
cards.back: A corner point of a feasible region is a point in the region which is the intersection of two boundary lines.
cards.quote: A corner point of a feasible region is a point in the region which is the intersection of two boundary lines.

source.section: Graphical method of solving linear programming problems

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: When is a feasible region said to be bounded?
cards.back: A feasible region of a system of linear inequalities is said to be bounded if it can be enclosed within a circle. Otherwise, it is called unbounded.
cards.quote: A feasible region of a system of linear inequalities is said to be bounded if it can be enclosed within a circle. Otherwise, it is called unbounded.

source.section: Graphical method of solving linear programming problems

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: What does an unbounded feasible region mean?
cards.back: Unbounded means that the feasible region does extend indefinitely in any direction.
cards.quote: Unbounded means that the feasible region does extend indefinitely in any direction.

source.section: Graphical method of solving linear programming problems

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: What follows when no point satisfies all the constraints simultaneously?
cards.back: Thus, the problem is having no feasible region and hence no feasible solution.
cards.quote: there is no point satisfying all the constraints simultaneously. Thus, the problem is having no feasible region and hence no feasible solution.

source.section: Graphical method of solving linear programming problems

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: The feasible region is always a ____ region.
cards.back: The feasible region is always a convex region.
cards.quote: The feasible region is always a convex region.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: If two corner points produce the same maximum (or minimum) value of the objective function, what about the points between them?
cards.back: every point on the line segment joining these points will also give the same maximum (or minimum) value.
cards.quote: If two corner points produce the same maximum (or minimum) value of the objective function, then every point on the line segment joining these points will also give the same maximum (or minimum) value.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Variables are sometimes called decision variables and are ____.
cards.back: Variables are sometimes called decision variables and are non-negative.
cards.quote: Variables are sometimes called decision variables and are non-negative.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: What is a matrix?
cards.back: A matrix is an ordered rectangular array of numbers or functions. The numbers or functions are called the elements or the entries of the matrix.
cards.quote: A matrix is an ordered rectangular array of numbers or functions. The numbers or functions are called the elements or the entries of the matrix.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: What is the order of a matrix?
cards.back: A matrix having m rows and n columns is called a matrix of order m × n or simply m × n matrix (read as an m by n matrix).
cards.quote: A matrix having m rows and n columns is called a matrix of order m × n or simply m × n matrix (read as an m by n matrix).

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: How many elements are there in an m × n matrix?
cards.back: The number of elements in an m × n matrix will be equal to mn.
cards.quote: The number of elements in an m × n matrix will be equal to mn.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: What is a column matrix?
cards.back: A matrix is said to be a column matrix if it has only one column.
cards.quote: A matrix is said to be a column matrix if it has only one column.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: What is a row matrix?
cards.back: A matrix is said to be a row matrix if it has only one row.
cards.quote: A matrix is said to be a row matrix if it has only one row.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: What is a square matrix?
cards.back: A matrix in which the number of rows are equal to the number of columns, is said to be a square matrix.
cards.quote: A matrix in which the number of rows are equal to the number of columns, is said to be a square matrix.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: When is an m × n matrix a square matrix, and what is its order then?
cards.back: Thus an m × n matrix is said to be a square matrix if m = n and is known as a square matrix of order ‘n’.
cards.quote: Thus an m × n matrix is said to be a square matrix if m = n and is known as a square matrix of order ‘n’.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: When is a diagonal matrix said to be a scalar matrix?
cards.back: A diagonal matrix is said to be a scalar matrix if its diagonal elements are equal
cards.quote: A diagonal matrix is said to be a scalar matrix if its diagonal elements are equal

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: What is an identity matrix?
cards.back: A square matrix in which elements in the diagonal are all 1 and rest are all zero is called an identity matrix.
cards.quote: A square matrix in which elements in the diagonal are all 1 and rest are all zero is called an identity matrix.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Is a scalar matrix an identity matrix, and is every identity matrix a scalar matrix?
cards.back: Observe that a scalar matrix is an identity matrix when k = 1. But every identity matrix is clearly a scalar matrix.
cards.quote: Observe that a scalar matrix is an identity matrix when k = 1. But every identity matrix is clearly a scalar matrix.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: What is a zero matrix (null matrix)?
cards.back: A matrix is said to be zero matrix or null matrix if all its elements are zero.
cards.quote: A matrix is said to be zero matrix or null matrix if all its elements are zero.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Two matrices A and B are equal if which two conditions hold?
cards.back:
(i) they are of the same order
(ii) each element of A is equal to the corresponding element of B
cards.quote:
(i) they are of the same order
(ii) each element of A is equal to the corresponding element of B

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Name the operations on matrices introduced in NCERT 3.4.
cards.back:
addition of matrices
multiplication of a matrix by a scalar
difference
multiplication of matrices
cards.quote: In this section, we shall introduce certain operations on matrices, namely, addition of matrices, multiplication of a matrix by a scalar, difference and multiplication of matrices.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: What is the sum of two matrices?
cards.back: The sum of two matrices is a matrix obtained by adding the corresponding elements of the given matrices. Furthermore, the two matrices have to be of the same order.
cards.quote: The sum of two matrices is a matrix obtained by adding the corresponding elements of the given matrices. Furthermore, the two matrices have to be of the same order.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: When is the sum A + B of two matrices not defined?
cards.back: We emphasise that if A and B are not of the same order, then A + B is not defined.
cards.quote: We emphasise that if A and B are not of the same order, then A + B is not defined.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: We may observe that addition of matrices is an example of ____ on the set of matrices of the same order.
cards.back: We may observe that addition of matrices is an example of binary operation on the set of matrices of the same order.
cards.quote: We may observe that addition of matrices is an example of binary operation on the set of matrices of the same order.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: How is a matrix A multiplied by a scalar k?
cards.back: kA is another matrix which is obtained by multiplying each element of A by the scalar k.
cards.quote: kA is another matrix which is obtained by multiplying each element of A by the scalar k.

source.section: Multiplication of a matrix by a scalar

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: When is the product of two matrices A and B defined?
cards.back: The product of two matrices A and B is defined if the number of columns of A is equal to the number of rows of B.
cards.quote: The product of two matrices A and B is defined if the number of columns of A is equal to the number of rows of B.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: If A is an m × n matrix and B is an n × p matrix, what is the order of the product AB?
cards.back: Then the product of the matrices A and B is the matrix C of order m × p.
cards.quote: Then the product of the matrices A and B is the matrix C of order m × p.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Furthermore for getting the elements of the product matrix, we take ____ and ____, multiply them element-wise and take the sum.
cards.back: Furthermore for getting the elements of the product matrix, we take rows of A and columns of B, multiply them element-wise and take the sum.
cards.quote: Furthermore for getting the elements of the product matrix, we take rows of A and columns of B, multiply them element-wise and take the sum.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: If AB is defined, is BA always defined?
cards.back: If AB is defined, then BA need not be defined.
cards.quote: If AB is defined, then BA need not be defined.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: When are both AB and BA defined for an m × n matrix A and a k × l matrix B?
cards.back: If A, B are, respectively m × n, k × l matrices, then both AB and BA are defined if and only if n = k and l = m.
cards.quote: If A, B are, respectively m × n, k × l matrices, then both AB and BA are defined if and only if n = k and l = m.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: If A and B are square matrices of the same order, are AB and BA both defined?
cards.back: In particular, if both A and B are square matrices of the same order, then both AB and BA are defined.
cards.quote: In particular, if both A and B are square matrices of the same order, then both AB and BA are defined.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: If the product of two matrices is a zero matrix, must one of the matrices be a zero matrix?
cards.back: Thus, if the product of two matrices is a zero matrix, it is not necessary that one of the matrices is a zero matrix.
cards.quote: Thus, if the product of two matrices is a zero matrix, it is not necessary that one of the matrices is a zero matrix.

source.section: Zero matrix as the product of two non zero matrices

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: What is the transpose of a matrix?
cards.back: The matrix obtained by interchanging the rows and columns of A is called the transpose of A.
cards.quote: The matrix obtained by interchanging the rows and columns of A is called the transpose of A.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: When is a matrix A a symmetric matrix?
cards.back: A is a symmetric matrix if A′ = A.
cards.quote: A is a symmetric matrix if A′ = A.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: When is a matrix A a skew symmetric matrix?
cards.back: A is a skew symmetric matrix if A′ = – A.
cards.quote: A is a skew symmetric matrix if A′ = – A.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: For a square matrix A with real entries, which of A + A′ and A – A′ is symmetric and which is skew symmetric?
cards.back: For any square matrix A with real number entries, A + A′ is a symmetric matrix and A – A′ is a skew symmetric matrix.
cards.quote: For any square matrix A with real number entries, A + A′ is a symmetric matrix and A – A′ is a skew symmetric matrix.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: How can any square matrix be expressed using symmetric and skew symmetric matrices?
cards.back: Any square matrix can be expressed as the sum of a symmetric and a skew symmetric matrix.
cards.quote: Any square matrix can be expressed as the sum of a symmetric and a skew symmetric matrix.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: What is the inverse of a square matrix A of order m?
cards.back: If A is a square matrix of order m, and if there exists another square matrix B of the same order m, such that AB = BA = I, then B is called the inverse matrix of A
cards.quote: If A is a square matrix of order m, and if there exists another square matrix B of the same order m, such that AB = BA = I, then B is called the inverse matrix of A
cards.note: A square matrix that has an inverse is called invertible.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Does a rectangular (non-square) matrix possess an inverse matrix?
cards.back: A rectangular matrix does not possess inverse matrix, since for products BA and AB to be defined and to be equal, it is necessary that matrices A and B should be square matrices of the same order.
cards.quote: A rectangular matrix does not possess inverse matrix, since for products BA and AB to be defined and to be equal, it is necessary that matrices A and B should be square matrices of the same order.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: If B is the inverse of A, what can be said about A?
cards.back: If B is the inverse of A, then A is also the inverse of B.
cards.quote: If B is the inverse of A, then A is also the inverse of B.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Uniqueness of inverse: how many inverses can a square matrix have?
cards.back: Inverse of a square matrix, if it exists, is unique.
cards.quote: Inverse of a square matrix, if it exists, is unique.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: What are independent events?
cards.back: Thus, E and F are two events such that the probability of occurrence of one of them is not affected by occurrence of the other. Such events are called independent events.
cards.quote: Thus, E and F are two events such that the probability of occurrence of one of them is not affected by occurrence of the other. Such events are called independent events.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: When are two events said to be dependent?
cards.back: Two events E and F are said to be dependent if they are not independent
cards.quote: Two events E and F are said to be dependent if they are not independent

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Independent vs mutually exclusive events: the difference on a common outcome.
cards.back: Moreover, mutually exclusive events never have an outcome common, but independent events, may have common outcome.
cards.quote: Moreover, mutually exclusive events never have an outcome common, but independent events, may have common outcome.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: When are two experiments said to be independent?
cards.back: Two experiments are said to be independent if for every pair of events E and F, where E is associated with the first experiment and F with the second experiment, the probability of the simultaneous occurrence of the events E and F when the two experiments are performed is the product of P(E) and P(F) calculated separately on the basis of two experiments
cards.quote: Two experiments are said to be independent if for every pair of events E and F, where E is associated with the first experiment and F with the second experiment, the probability of the simultaneous occurrence of the events E and F when the two experiments are performed is the product of P(E) and P(F) calculated separately on the basis of two experiments

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Bayes' theorem is also called the formula for the probability of "____".
cards.back: Bayes' theorem is also called the formula for the probability of "causes".
cards.quote: Bayes' theorem is also called the formula for the probability of "causes".

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: What is a random variable?
cards.back: A random variable is a real valued function whose domain is the sample space of a random experiment.
cards.quote: A random variable is a real valued function whose domain is the sample space of a random experiment.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: As seen in Class XI, functions are special kind of ____.
cards.back: As seen in Class XI, functions are special kind of relations.
cards.quote: As seen in Class XI, functions are special kind of relations.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Define an empty relation R in a set A.
cards.back: A relation R in a set A is called empty relation, if no element of A is related to any element of A
cards.quote: A relation R in a set A is called empty relation, if no element of A is related to any element of A

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: A relation R in a set A is called ____ relation, if no element of A is related to any element of A
cards.back: A relation R in a set A is called empty relation, if no element of A is related to any element of A
cards.quote: A relation R in a set A is called empty relation, if no element of A is related to any element of A

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Define a universal relation R in a set A.
cards.back: A relation R in a set A is called universal relation, if each element of A is related to every element of A
cards.quote: A relation R in a set A is called universal relation, if each element of A is related to every element of A

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: A relation R in a set A is called ____ relation, if each element of A is related to every element of A
cards.back: A relation R in a set A is called universal relation, if each element of A is related to every element of A
cards.quote: A relation R in a set A is called universal relation, if each element of A is related to every element of A

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Both the empty relation and the universal relation are sometimes called ____ relations.
cards.back: Both the empty relation and the universal relation are sometimes called trivial relations.
cards.quote: Both the empty relation and the universal relation are sometimes called trivial relations.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Name the three types of relations considered first to study equivalence relation.
cards.back:
reflexive
symmetric
transitive
cards.quote: To study equivalence relation, we first consider three types of relations, namely reflexive, symmetric and transitive.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Define an equivalence relation R in a set A.
cards.back: A relation R in a set A is said to be an equivalence relation if R is reflexive, symmetric and transitive.
cards.quote: A relation R in a set A is said to be an equivalence relation if R is reflexive, symmetric and transitive.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: A relation R in a set A is said to be an ____ if R is reflexive, symmetric and transitive.
cards.back: A relation R in a set A is said to be an equivalence relation if R is reflexive, symmetric and transitive.
cards.quote: A relation R in a set A is said to be an equivalence relation if R is reflexive, symmetric and transitive.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: For the relation 'the difference of a and b is divisible by 2' on integers, which integers are related to zero?
cards.back: note that all even integers are related to zero
cards.quote: note that all even integers are related to zero

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: For the relation 'the difference of a and b is divisible by 2' on integers, which integers are related to one?
cards.back: all odd integers are related to one and no even integer is related to one
cards.quote: all odd integers are related to one and no even integer is related to one

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: For the relation 'the difference of a and b is divisible by 2' on integers, what is the subset E of even integers called?
cards.back: The subset E is called the equivalence class containing zero
cards.quote: The subset E is called the equivalence class containing zero

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Given an arbitrary equivalence relation R in an arbitrary set X, R divides X into mutually ____ subsets
cards.back: Given an arbitrary equivalence relation R in an arbitrary set X, R divides X into mutually disjoint subsets
cards.quote: Given an arbitrary equivalence relation R in an arbitrary set X, R divides X into mutually disjoint subsets

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Define the equivalence class [a] containing a in X for an equivalence relation R in X.
cards.back: the subset of X containing all elements b related to a
cards.quote: is the subset of X containing all elements b related to a

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Define a one-one (injective) function f : X → Y.
cards.back: A function f : X → Y is defined to be one-one (or injective), if the images of distinct elements of X under f are distinct
cards.quote: A function f : X → Y is defined to be one-one (or injective), if the images of distinct elements of X under f are distinct

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: If a function f is not one-one, what is it called?
cards.back: many-one
cards.quote: Otherwise, f is called many-one.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Define an onto (surjective) function f : X → Y.
cards.back: A function f : X → Y is said to be onto (or surjective), if every element of Y is the image of some element of X under f
cards.quote: A function f : X → Y is said to be onto (or surjective), if every element of Y is the image of some element of X under f

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: A function f : X → Y is said to be ____ (or surjective), if every element of Y is the image of some element of X under f
cards.back: A function f : X → Y is said to be onto (or surjective), if every element of Y is the image of some element of X under f
cards.quote: A function f : X → Y is said to be onto (or surjective), if every element of Y is the image of some element of X under f

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Define a bijective function f : X → Y.
cards.back: A function f : X → Y is said to be one-one and onto (or bijective), if f is both one-one and onto.
cards.quote: A function f : X → Y is said to be one-one and onto (or bijective), if f is both one-one and onto.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: A function f : X → Y is said to be one-one and onto (or ____), if f is both one-one and onto.
cards.back: A function f : X → Y is said to be one-one and onto (or bijective), if f is both one-one and onto.
cards.quote: A function f : X → Y is said to be one-one and onto (or bijective), if f is both one-one and onto.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: For every finite set X, how are one-one and onto related for a function from X to X?
cards.back: a one-one function f : X → X is necessarily onto and an onto map f : X → X is necessarily one-one, for every finite set X
cards.quote: a one-one function f : X → X is necessarily onto and an onto map f : X → X is necessarily one-one, for every finite set X

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Does 'one-one implies onto' for a map from X to X hold for an infinite set?
cards.back: for an infinite set, this may not be true
cards.quote: In contrast to this, Examples 8 and 10 show that for an infinite set, this may not be true.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Define direction cosines of a line.
cards.back: Direction cosines of a line are the cosines of the angles made by the line with the positive directions of the coordinate axes.
cards.quote: Direction cosines of a line are the cosines of the angles made by the line with the positive directions of the coordinate axes.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: If we reverse the direction of L, then the direction angles are replaced by their ____
cards.back: If we reverse the direction of L, then the direction angles are replaced by their supplements
cards.quote: If we reverse the direction of L, then the direction angles are replaced by their supplements

source.section: 11.2 Direction Cosines and Direction Ratios of a Line

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: What happens to the signs of the direction cosines when the direction of a line is reversed?
cards.back: Thus, the signs of the direction cosines are reversed.
cards.quote: Thus, the signs of the direction cosines are reversed.

source.section: 11.2 Direction Cosines and Direction Ratios of a Line

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: How many sets of direction cosines does a given line in space have, and why?
cards.back: Note that a given line in space can be extended in two opposite directions and so it has two sets of direction cosines.
cards.quote: Note that a given line in space can be extended in two opposite directions and so it has two sets of direction cosines.

source.section: 11.2 Direction Cosines and Direction Ratios of a Line

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: In order to have a unique set of direction cosines for a given line in space, we must take the given line as a ____ line.
cards.back: In order to have a unique set of direction cosines for a given line in space, we must take the given line as a directed line.
