cards.quote: In order to have a unique set of direction cosines for a given line in space, we must take the given line as a directed line.

source.section: 11.2 Direction Cosines and Direction Ratios of a Line

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: How are the unique direction cosines of a directed line denoted?
cards.back: These unique direction cosines are denoted by l, m and n.
cards.quote: These unique direction cosines are denoted by l, m and n.

source.section: 11.2 Direction Cosines and Direction Ratios of a Line

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Steps to find the direction cosines of a line that does not pass through the origin.
cards.back:
we draw a line through the origin and parallel to the given line.
Now take one of the directed lines from the origin and find its direction cosines
cards.quote: If the given line in space does not pass through the origin, then, in order to find its direction cosines, we draw a line through the origin and parallel to the given line. Now take one of the directed lines from the origin and find its direction cosines

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: What do two parallel lines have in common regarding direction cosines?
cards.back: two parallel line have same set of direction cosines
cards.quote: two parallel line have same set of direction cosines

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Define direction ratios of a line.
cards.back: Any three numbers which are proportional to the direction cosines of a line are called the direction ratios of the line.
cards.quote: Any three numbers which are proportional to the direction cosines of a line are called the direction ratios of the line.

source.section: 11.2 Direction Cosines and Direction Ratios of a Line

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: What are the direction cosines of the x-axis?

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: What are the direction cosines of the y-axis and the z-axis?
cards.back: direction cosines of y-axis and z-axis are 0, 1, 0 and 0, 0, 1 respectively.
cards.quote: direction cosines of y-axis and z-axis are 0, 1, 0 and 0, 0, 1 respectively.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: A line in space is uniquely determined in which two ways?
cards.back: (i) it passes through a given point and has given direction, or (ii) it passes through two given points.
cards.quote: A line is uniquely determined if (i) it passes through a given point and has given direction, or (ii) it passes through two given points.

source.section: 11.3 Equation of a Line in Space

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: If a vector parallel to a line has components a, b and c along the three axes, what are a, b and c for the line?
cards.back: direction ratios of the line
cards.quote: then a, b, c are direction ratios of the line

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Define skew lines.
cards.back: Skew lines are lines in space which are neither parallel nor intersecting.
cards.quote: Skew lines are lines in space which are neither parallel nor intersecting.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Do skew lines lie in the same plane?
cards.back: They lie in different planes.
cards.quote: They lie in different planes.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Define the angle between skew lines.
cards.back: Angle between skew lines is the angle between two intersecting lines drawn from any point (preferably through the origin) parallel to each of the skew lines.
cards.quote: Angle between skew lines is the angle between two intersecting lines drawn from any point (preferably through the origin) parallel to each of the skew lines.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: If two lines in space intersect at a point, then the shortest distance between them is ____.
cards.back: If two lines in space intersect at a point, then the shortest distance between them is zero.
cards.quote: If two lines in space intersect at a point, then the shortest distance between them is zero.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: What is meant by the shortest distance between two lines?
cards.back: By the shortest distance between two lines we mean the join of a point in one line with one point on the other line so that the length of the segment so obtained is the smallest.
cards.quote: By the shortest distance between two lines we mean the join of a point in one line with one point on the other line so that the length of the segment so obtained is the smallest.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: For skew lines, the line of the shortest distance will be ____ to both the lines.
cards.back: For skew lines, the line of the shortest distance will be perpendicular to both the lines.
cards.quote: For skew lines, the line of the shortest distance will be perpendicular to both the lines.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Define the shortest distance between two skew lines.
cards.back: Shortest distance between two skew lines is the line segment perpendicular to both the lines.
cards.quote: Shortest distance between two skew lines is the line segment perpendicular to both the lines.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Define a scalar quantity.
cards.back: a quantity that involves only one value (magnitude) which is a real number. Such quantities are called scalars.
cards.quote: a quantity that involves only one value (magnitude) which is a real number. Such quantities are called scalars.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Name the scalar quantities NCERT lists as examples.
cards.back:
length
mass
time
distance
speed
area
volume
temperature
work
money
voltage
density
resistance
cards.quote: scalar quantities such as length, mass, time, distance, speed, area, volume, temperature, work, money, voltage, density, resistance etc.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Name the vector quantities NCERT lists as examples.
cards.back:
displacement
velocity
acceleration
force
weight
momentum
electric field intensity
cards.quote: vector quantities like displacement, velocity, acceleration, force, weight, momentum, electric field intensity etc.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Define a vector.
cards.back: A quantity that has magnitude as well as direction is called a vector.
cards.quote: A quantity that has magnitude as well as direction is called a vector.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Define the initial point and the terminal point of a vector.
cards.back: The point A from where the vector starts is called its initial point, and the point B where it ends is called its terminal point.
cards.quote: The point A from where the vector starts is called its initial point, and the point B where it ends is called its terminal point.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Define the magnitude (or length) of a vector.
cards.back: The distance between initial and terminal points of a vector is called the magnitude (or length) of the vector
cards.quote: The distance between initial and terminal points of a vector is called the magnitude (or length) of the vector

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Define the position vector of a point P with respect to the origin O.
cards.back: Then, the vector having O and P as its initial and terminal points, respectively, is called the position vector of the point P with respect to O.
cards.quote: Then, the vector having O and P as its initial and terminal points, respectively, is called the position vector of the point P with respect to O.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: What are the cosines of the direction angles of a vector called, and which letters usually denote them?
cards.back: direction cosines of the vector, and usually denoted by l, m and n, respectively.
cards.quote: direction cosines of the vector, and usually denoted by l, m and n, respectively.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Define a zero vector (or null vector).
cards.back: A vector whose initial and terminal points coincide, is called a zero vector (or null vector)
cards.quote: A vector whose initial and terminal points coincide, is called a zero vector (or null vector)

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Zero vector can not be assigned a ____ as it has zero magnitude.
cards.back: Zero vector can not be assigned a definite direction as it has zero magnitude.
cards.quote: Zero vector can not be assigned a definite direction as it has zero magnitude.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Define a unit vector.
cards.back: A vector whose magnitude is unity (i.e., 1 unit) is called a unit vector.
cards.quote: A vector whose magnitude is unity (i.e., 1 unit) is called a unit vector.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Define coinitial vectors.
cards.back: Two or more vectors having the same initial point are called coinitial vectors.
cards.quote: Two or more vectors having the same initial point are called coinitial vectors.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: When are two or more vectors said to be collinear?
cards.back: Two or more vectors are said to be collinear if they are parallel to the same line, irrespective of their magnitudes and directions.
cards.quote: Two or more vectors are said to be collinear if they are parallel to the same line, irrespective of their magnitudes and directions.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: When are two vectors said to be equal?
cards.back: Two vectors are said to be equal, if they have the same magnitude and direction regardless of the positions of their initial points
cards.quote: Two vectors are said to be equal, if they have the same magnitude and direction regardless of the positions of their initial points

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: What are vectors that may be shifted by parallel displacement without changing magnitude and direction called?
cards.back: The vectors defined above are such that any of them may be subject to its parallel displacement without changing its magnitude and direction. Such vectors are called free vectors.
cards.quote: The vectors defined above are such that any of them may be subject to its parallel displacement without changing its magnitude and direction. Such vectors are called free vectors.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: A girl moves from A to B and then from B to C. The net displacement from A to C is the sum of the two vectors. Which law is this?
cards.back: This is known as the triangle law of vector addition.
cards.quote: This is known as the triangle law of vector addition.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: In the triangle law, how are two vectors positioned in order to add them?
cards.back: to add them, they are positioned so that the initial point of one coincides with the terminal point of the other
cards.quote: to add them, they are positioned so that the initial point of one coincides with the terminal point of the other

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: If two vectors are the adjacent sides of a parallelogram in magnitude and direction, by what is their sum represented? Name the law.
cards.back: then their sum is represented in magnitude and direction by the diagonal of the parallelogram through their common point. This is known as the parallelogram law of vector addition.
cards.quote: then their sum is represented in magnitude and direction by the diagonal of the parallelogram through their common point. This is known as the parallelogram law of vector addition.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: The ____ of vector addition enables us to write the sum of three vectors without using brackets.
cards.back: The associative property of vector addition enables us to write the sum of three vectors without using brackets.
cards.quote: The associative property of vector addition enables us to write the sum of three vectors without using brackets.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: What are the vectors of magnitude 1 along the axes OX, OY and OZ called (denoted by i, j and k with hats)?
cards.back: each having magnitude 1, are called unit vectors along the axes OX, OY and OZ, respectively
cards.quote: each having magnitude 1, are called unit vectors along the axes OX, OY and OZ, respectively

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: How is the length of a vector in component form (with scalar components x, y and z) readily determined?
cards.back: by applying the Pythagoras theorem twice
cards.quote: is readily determined by applying the Pythagoras theorem twice.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Note that two vectors are equal if and only if their ____ are equal.
cards.back: Note that two vectors are equal if and only if their corresponding components are equal.
cards.quote: Note that two vectors are equal if and only if their corresponding components are equal.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: The scalar components of a vector are its ____, and represent its projections along the respective axes.
cards.back: The scalar components of a vector are its direction ratios, and represent its projections along the respective axes.
cards.quote: The scalar components of a vector are its direction ratios, and represent its projections along the respective axes.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: In the section formula, what is the relation between m and n when R is the midpoint of PQ?
cards.back: If R is the midpoint of PQ, then m = n.
cards.quote: If R is the midpoint of PQ, then m = n.

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: We know that two nonzero vectors are perpendicular if their ____ is zero.
cards.back: We know that two nonzero vectors are perpendicular if their scalar product is zero.
cards.quote: We know that two nonzero vectors are perpendicular if their scalar product is zero.

source.section: 10.6.1 Scalar (or dot) product of two vectors

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Property 1 of the scalar product (a vector dotted with a sum of two others) is called what?
cards.back: Distributivity of scalar product over addition
cards.quote: Distributivity of scalar product over addition

source.section: 10.6.1 Scalar (or dot) product of two vectors

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: In a right handed coordinate system, where does the thumb point when the fingers curl from the positive x-axis toward the positive y-axis?
cards.back: the thumb of the right hand points in the direction of the positive z-axis
cards.quote: In a right handed coordinate system, the thumb of the right hand points in the direction of the positive z-axis when the fingers are curled in the direction away from the positive x-axis toward the positive y-axis

source.section: 10.6.3 Vector (or cross) product of two vectors

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: Property 3 of the vector product, valid for any three vectors and a scalar, is called what?
cards.back: Distributivity of vector product over addition
cards.quote: Distributivity of vector product over addition

source.section: 10.6.3 Vector (or cross) product of two vectors

cards.subject: mathematics
cards.front: The vector sum of two coinitial vectors is given by the ____ of the parallelogram whose adjacent sides are the given vectors.
cards.back: The vector sum of two coinitial vectors is given by the diagonal of the parallelogram whose adjacent sides are the given vectors.
cards.quote: The vector sum of two coinitial vectors is given by the diagonal of the parallelogram whose adjacent sides are the given vectors.
